items.stem: A policy was introduced in some regions but not others at the same time. Comparing before-and-after changes across the two groups uses which design?

options.rationale: Correct: difference-in-differences compares the change over time between treated and untreated groups.
A simple correlation does not isolate the policy's effect.
Random sampling concerns who is surveyed, not identification.

options.text: A single pre/post comparison in one group
options.rationale: A single-group pre/post comparison cannot separate the policy from other time trends.

items.explanation: Correct: difference-in-differences compares the change over time between treated and untreated groups.

items.stem: Why can regression adjustment still give a biased causal estimate even with many controls?

options.text: It cannot adjust for confounders that were not measured
options.rationale: Correct: regression can only adjust for observed covariates, leaving unmeasured confounding.
Overfitting is a separate concern and not the core issue here.
Regression does not require randomization to run.

options.text: It only works on time series
options.rationale: Regression is not limited to time series.

items.explanation: Correct: regression can only adjust for observed covariates, leaving unmeasured confounding.

items.stem: Which TWO are conditions for a valid instrumental variable? (Select TWO)

options.text: It is associated with the treatment (relevance)
options.rationale: Correct: relevance requires the instrument to influence the treatment.

options.text: It affects the outcome only through the treatment (exclusion)
options.rationale: Correct: the exclusion restriction requires the instrument to affect the outcome only via the treatment.

options.text: It must be the outcome itself
options.rationale: An instrument is distinct from the outcome.

options.text: It must be randomly measured error
options.rationale: An instrument is a variable with specific properties, not measurement error.

items.explanation: Correct: relevance requires the instrument to influence the treatment.; Correct: the exclusion restriction requires the instrument to affect the outcome only via the treatment.
